title: Progressive virtualization and priority-aware column collapse for dense data grids
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background:
Many product teams load very wide and deep grids (50+ columns, thousands of rows) which makes current virtualization + manual column resizing/collapse workflows fragile: slow initial paint, janky resize, and difficult keyboard/assistive navigation when columns change width or are hidden. Existing tickets addressed column-resize and density gestures, but we still see recurring support tickets asking for an automatic way to preserve important columns and gracefully collapse less important ones when space is constrained.

Goal:
Design and spec a pattern called "priority-aware column collapse" paired with a progressive virtualization strategy that: 1) keeps key columns visible by policy (pin, priority score) 2) progressively reduces render cost by lowering row granularity and placeholder fidelity at extreme densities and offscreen ranges 3) exposes clear user controls to override automatic collapse 4) preserves keyboard navigation and screen-reader semantics throughout transitions.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Non-goal: full rewrite of grid engine or virtualization runtime. We must work with existing React virtualization primitives (windowing / list virtualization) and the runtime team’s chunked rendering strategy.
- Must work with existing tokens for spacing/typography and with density modes (compact/regular/comfortable).
- Should not change API surface for consumers except for opt-in flags and a small JSON column metadata shape.

Proposed UX:
1) Column metadata: introduce optional column attribute `priority: 0..3` and `collapseGroup` (string). By default most columns are priority 1. UI: in column settings menu designers can mark as "Essential" (priority 3) or add to a named group.
2) Adaptive collapse policy: when table width < threshold for all columns, apply rules: keep all priority 3, start collapsing priority 0 then 1 within lowest significance groups. Collapse operation is first-to-group, not per column, with a tooltip showing which columns were collapsed.
3) Progressive virtualization: render pipeline stages depending on on-screen distance and density mode: full row cells for visible viewport, skeleton/placeholder rows at +/- 1 viewport, simplified DOM (text nodes only, no interactive affordances) beyond that. At extreme virtualized states (very high row counts) we can render even lighter placeholder rows (single-row height approximations) to limit layout cost.
4) Sticky interactive header: header becomes a compact toolbar at narrow widths with an explicit "Reveal hidden columns" affordance that shows collapsed columns in a transient flyout. Header toolbar should include column reorder handle, quick density menu, and per-column settings.
5) Manual override: collapsed columns are still addressable via column settings or the flyout; users can pin/unpin to change priority. Pinning is sticky per user and can be toggled by product teams via the column metadata API.
6) Animations & transitions: soft cross-fade for placeholder → full-rendered rows; slide-and-scale for column collapse to preserve spatial context. All animations are preference-aware (reduce-motion respects OS-level setting).

Accessibility & Keyboard:
- Keyboard: preserved tab order across collapse; when a column is collapsed keyboard focus moves to the first remaining cell in that row. Provide a keyboard shortcut to open the collapsed-columns flyout (Ctrl+Alt+C).
- Screen readers: announce when columns are auto-collapsed ("3 columns collapsed: Actions, Notes, Tags") and expose the flyout via ARIA dialog role. Collapsed columns remain readable via screen-reader toggle.

Acceptance criteria (designer + eng):
- Interaction spec with annotated flows (Figma file link) covering <1> auto-collapse threshold, <2> manual overrides, <3> flyout behavior, <4> keyboard flows.
- Implementation shim/API: optional column metadata shape documented in API guide; default behavior is opt-in.
- Performance target: initial table paint (first meaningful paint) for 10k rows x 30 cols reduced by at least 30% in progressive virtualization mode compared to baseline.
- UX tolerances: collapse/expand completes within 200ms for common collapse sets (<=5 columns) on mid-range devices.
- Accessibility checklist: keyboard flows verified, screen-reader announcements validated, reduce-motion honored.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should priority be numeric or enumerated string? (We prefer numeric for easier server-driven scoring, but will prototype both.)
- How aggressive should automatic collapse be for responsive breakpoints vs user-controlled density mode? We propose automatic collapse only when width < 900px or when density is compact + user toggles automatic collapse.
- Server vs client decisioning: recommend client-side with optional server-provided priority hints for enterprise use (faster mount decisions).

Work needed / handoffs:
- Design: finalize Figma screens, micro-interaction specs, token mapping for compact/regular/comfortable.
- Engineering (frontend): implement column metadata parsing, flyout component, and progressive render stages; coordinate with runtime team for virtualization chunk sizes.
- Engineering (platform): document opt-in column metadata in our public API docs and update SDK examples.
- QA: performance regression harness (10k x 50 grid scenarios) and accessibility regression tests.

References / artifacts:
- Figma draft: https://www.figma.com/file/fakeid/progressive-virtualization (private)
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood/example/prog-virt (internal)
- Perf dashboard baseline: https://dashboards.redwood/perf/grid-baseline-2025
- Prototype PR (proof-of-concept): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/4125

Notes for follow-up:
- Short-term: ship an opt-in beta toggle in Console for product teams to preview non-invasive collapse.
- Mid-term: collaborate with runtime team to explore a runtime hint (visibleColumnSet) that precomputes columns to render server-side for private deployments.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Frequency of auto-collapse events (per table type)
- Rate of manual override (pin/unpin) — signals policy accuracy
- First-meaningful-paint and TTFB for large tables
- Accessibility regressions reported
